1) collective inference is not always beneficial, 2) collective inference can be beneficial even when the underlying statistical models are identical, and 3) when collective inference is beneficial, it is due to the presence of statistical dependencies in the underlying data, not the statistical model used for inference.

the problem of relational classification and the question of when collective inference can be expected to reduce error.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in general, the use of collective inference is a necessary and sufficient condition for reduced error when compared with individual classification, and that the use of a collective inference algorithm is a sufficient condition for reduced classification error when compared to a traditional inference technique.
the collective inference approach is more accurate because it is a more flexible approach to inference that can better capture the underlying structure of relational data.

collective inference improves classification accuracy in relational data if and only if (1) the data is relational, (2) the data contains a significant amount of inter-instance dependency, and (3) the data has a significant amount of noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
collective inference is a powerful approach for classification in relational data, but the benefits are not guaranteed.
collective inference improves classification accuracy when the underlying statistical models for the data are similar for the different instances.
collective inference can reduce classification error if and only if the data are highly correlated and if there is a high probability of error in the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for certain relational models, collective inference can reduce error by exploiting the redundancy of information in the data.

collective inference can reduce classification error when the underlying model of relational data has the property that the probability of a relational instance depends on the class label for other related data instances.

the error reduction is a result of a combination of two factors: (1) the use of relational information in making inference about individual data items and (2) the use of collective inference to make simultaneous judgments about the same set of data items.
